features.title: Public API
features.tldr: rand_engine exports DataGenerator, SparkGenerator and RandSpecs; every other module is internal.
features.summary: The supported import surface is the three names in rand_engine.__all__, plus the RandEngineError exception family a caller catches; the wheel ships only the rand_engine package.

features.title: Templates and examples
features.tldr: Ready RandSpecs — ten cross-engine CommonRandSpecs, ten pandas-only AdvancedRandSpecs, and a UTC WebServerLogs template.
features.summary: Prebuilt specs a user runs without writing a grammar — CommonRandSpecs is exported as RandSpecs and runs on both generators; AdvancedRandSpecs demonstrates correlated pandas methods; WebServerLogs assembles Apache common log lines in UTC.

features.title: DataGenerator
features.tldr: The pandas generator validates a RandSpec, owns its random generator, and returns DataFrames, files, file streams or an endless record stream.
features.summary: DataGenerator(spec, seed) is the pandas composition root; size and transformers feed get_df, stream_dict, write and writeStream, with one owned NumPy generator and row offsets that keep keys continuous across stream batches and file parts.

features.title: Generation methods
features.tldr: Ten common methods run on pandas and Spark; four correlated methods plus pk and fk run on pandas.
features.summary: NPCore and PyCore provide the NumPy generator's single method map, including deterministic keys; SparkCore supplies native Spark expressions for the ten common methods.

features.title: SparkGenerator
features.tldr: The Spark generator builds a Spark DataFrame from common RandSpec methods with native expressions and no Python UDF.
features.summary: SparkGenerator(spark, F, spec) validates the common grammar, starts from spark.range(size), adds native SparkCore columns and refuses the NumPy-only pk and fk methods.

features.title: Writers and streaming
features.tldr: DataGenerator writes CSV, JSON lines and Parquet batches or repeated file-stream microbatches through a Spark-style builder.
features.summary: The batch writer distributes one requested total row count across numFiles; the stream writer emits size rows per microbatch. CSV and Parquet use PyArrow, JSON uses pandas, and each format accepts only documented options.

features.title: Performance benchmarks
features.tldr: A CI-only same-runner A/B benchmark measures every generation method and built-in sink, publishes its table and enforces a relative regression limit.
features.summary: The benchmark coordinator alternates timed requests between long-lived base and head workers per row, reports method and sink throughput, publishes Markdown and JSON artifacts, and fails when a comparable head row exceeds the configured ratio.

features.title: PK/FK key columns
features.tldr: Stateless pk and fk column methods create related tables from definitions, seeds and row indexes without a checkpoint store.
features.summary: A pk is a sequence or a deterministic permutation of row indexes; an fk deterministically selects a parent row and rebuilds its pk value. Batch parts and stream microbatches advance row offsets, so keys remain consistent without shared state.

features.title: RandSpec grammar
features.tldr: A RandSpec maps output columns to a method, named kwargs and optional multi-column or transformer metadata, and is validated before generation.
features.summary: AdvancedValidator validates NumPy common, correlated and key methods; CommonValidator validates the Spark common-method subset. Args and top-level constraints are refused, and validation collects issues into SpecValidationError.
